$comment: Gate 1 (devolt memory/decisions/2026-09-25-brownout-core-w1-plan.md, section
3.4.1; core/README.md's contract). Every test case in every suite file
wired into vitest.core-suites.config.ts's `test.include` is listed here,
classified as one of:
- "portable":     runs on the core for the kinds it uses; wired into
vitest.core-suites.config.ts's testNamePattern.
- "classic-only":  pins a classic-internal detail (step counts, Newton
iteration counts, engine.state, captureErrorState,
a split) that has no core counterpart and is not
part of the accuracy contract; never runs on the core.
- "not-yet":       every kind the test's circuit uses is real device
behaviour, but at least one of those kinds has not
been ported to the core yet (or, for a handful of
kinds below, is not in the W1 plan's kind table at
all -- diode/bjt_npn/nmos/lm358/microbit).
`kinds` lists every SimComponent.kind the test's circuit instantiates
(excluding the implicit ground net). gate-reporter.ts sums, per kind, how
many "portable" cases actually ran and passed under this file's
testNamePattern, and fails the whole run if any kind named in a portable
case's `kinds` array has a count of zero for that file -- see its own
header comment for why this must be computed from portable entries only,
not from CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS (which also contains "ground", a compiler-
internal detail no test ever names as a component kind). It ALSO fails
when any CORE_IMPLEMENTED_KINDS member except "ground" has no portable
case, in any file, that ran and passed (the coverage floor, W1b review
finding 9): a kind the core implements must be exercised here.

cases.describe: reference physics — RC step response at multiple timesteps
cases.name: h=tau/100 stays within 0.3% full-scale at t=tau
cases.reason: Single capacitor, one partition (closed form, W1b step 2). The assertion compares classic's own step result against the ANALYTIC exponential with a tolerance sized for classic's own discretization error at this h; the core's closed-form evaluation is exact (no discretization), so it clears the same (looser) bound. The pre-step voltage this case reloads from is 0 V on both engines regardless of whether a full bo_engine_load carries capacitor state forward the way classic's own load() does, so the case does not depend on that being true. NOTE ON MATCHING: the RC and RL step-response describe blocks share IDENTICAL it() titles (h=tau/100 / h=tau/20 / h=tau/10), so gate 1 matches every case on its FULL name, `describe` + " " + `name` (vitest's own testNamePattern join), anchored at both ends -- a bare it()-title match would also select the not-yet inductor RL cases below.

cases.describe: reference physics — transient KCL/KVL and energy residuals
cases.name: RC companion satisfies KCL and its discrete energy identity
cases.reason: Reconstructs `capacitorCurrent = capacitance * (voltage - previousVoltage) / h` and checks a KCL residual against it -- a property of classic's own fixed-h backward-Euler finite difference, not of the device's continuous physics. The core's single-capacitor partition (W1b step 2) advances the closed form continuously (no per-step h to reconstruct a matching discrete derivative from), so this identity is not a like-for-like comparison there. Forcing the core's generic stepped path (FORCE_STEPPED, core/README.md's Options table) would make the two arithmetically comparable again -- but the gate-1 adapter (test/core/suites/adapter.ts) is built on HeadlessRunner, and HeadlessRunnerOptions/HeadlessRunOptions carry no compile-options passthrough (no forceStepped, no CompileOptions of any kind) -- so there is currently no way to route this specific case's assertion onto the core's stepped path through this harness. A future worker could add that passthrough (HeadlessRunnerOptions.compileOptions, threaded into CoreEngine.load's options) to lift this to "portable" under FORCE_STEPPED.

cases.describe: spdt_switch.updateCurrent — Q-O26 (com to the contact in use)
cases.name: position 0 (com->b active, b floating with no load) reports ~0 A: no complete circuit
cases.reason: com is fixed (wired directly to the source) and b is the device's only OTHER free pin (c has no wire to it either in this case's own rig, since r1 sits on c) -- wait, r1 is wired to c even here, so b and c are the device's two free contacts in potentially different partitions (com fixed, so nothing unions them, per finding 1). The ACTIVE contact at position 0 is com-b, and b's own partition IS the device's attributed owner (owner_of picks the first free pin among [com,b,c] in declared order, i.e. b) -- so this reads the owning partition's own contact, not a cross-partition one, and is unaffected by finding 1's cross-partition mis-stamp.

cases.describe: spdt_switch.updateCurrent — Q-O26 (com to the contact in use)
cases.name: position 1 (com->c active, c loaded through r1) reports the real ~5 mA load current — THIS is the case that read 5000 A before the fix
cases.reason: com fixed; b and c are two DIFFERENT free-node partitions (b isolated, c loaded through r1) with the device's Owner attributed to b (the first free pin), exactly finding 1's cross-partition scenario -- but this circuit has no capacitor anywhere, so both partitions are Static, and the static solver evidently solves the whole static graph as one combined system rather than per-partition with local indexing (finding 1's fixed[node].unwrap_or(0.0) fabrication is specific to the dynamic ClosedForm/Stepped compile_dyn_shape path). Verified empirically against the built core: this reports the correct ~5 mA, not a fabricated-0V-driven phantom current.

cases.reason: A switch-gated RC: closed, the capacitor charges through 1 mOhm (tau about 1 ns) in a closed-form partition; open, the node never moves. Exercises a switch stamp inside a dynamic partition.
